question: Which of the following is NOT a valid category of alignment in Microsoft Word?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vertical.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Microsoft Word was first released in **1983**. It was originally developed for **MS-DOS** and later adapted for other operating systems.
 
• Microsoft Word uses a **Ribbon interface** where all commands are organized into tabs like Home, Insert, and Layout, making it user-friendly.
 
• Word documents are saved with the extension** .docx**, which is the default format in newer versions. It also supports older formats like **.doc** for compatibility.
 
• The Find feature **(Ctrl + F)** helps in locating specific words, while Replace (Ctrl + H) allows for replacing text quickly throughout the document.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Left Alignment:** This is the default alignment in Word where text is aligned to the left margin while the right edge remains uneven.
 
• **Right Alignment:** Text is aligned to the right margin, and the left edge is uneven, commonly used for numbering and headers.
 
• **Justify Alignment:** Text is spaced to align with both the left and right margins, creating a clean block of text on both sides.
 
• Word allows users to apply predefined styles for headings, paragraphs, and text for **consistent formatting**, which is essential in creating professional documents.
 
• The **Track Changes** feature allows users to track edits made in a document, making it useful for reviewing and collaborating on documents.
 
• The** Mail Merge** feature helps create personalized documents like letters or labels by linking a Word document with a data source** (like Excel) **for mass distribution.
